# 1. Overview

This notebook draws the **ATPα-focused** host-use figure: the three-state
host-use reconstruction (`none` / milkweed clade / native-range *Asclepias*)
restricted to the Danaini with a known ATPα genotype, with an inner ATPα strip.

It does **not** refit the model. The ancestral reconstruction is read from Figure 1
(`../../Figure1/output_data/host_use_milkweed_asclepias_ASR_node_probabilities.csv`),
and each focused internal node reuses the whole-tree probability of the
corresponding full-tree node (the MRCA of the same tips). Figure 1 must therefore be
rendered first.

Because the node probabilities are keyed by the full tree's internal node numbers,
this notebook rebuilds the full tree exactly as Figure 1 does — read, clean tip
labels, collapse internal branches with bootstrap support below `SUPPORT_CUTOFF`
(70) into polytomies, then rotate to the curated reference order — so the node
numbering lines up. A guard checks that the reconstruction's node set matches the
rebuilt tree before any pies are drawn.

Inputs (copied from Extended Data Figure 1, same files Figure 1 uses) live in
`../input_data/`; the focused figure is written to `../visuals/` and the focused
node probabilities to `../output_data/`.

```{r setup, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

library(tidyverse)
library(ape)
library(ggtree)
library(ggnewscale)

dir.create("../output_data", showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create("../visuals", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Path to the whole-tree reconstruction produced by Figure 1.
asr_source <- "../../Figure1/output_data/host_use_milkweed_asclepias_ASR_node_probabilities.csv"

clean_name <- function(x) {
  stringr::str_squish(stringr::str_replace_all(as.character(x), "_", " "))
}

# "Danaus plexippus" -> "D. plexippus" for tip labels
abbr_tip <- function(x) {
  x <- clean_name(x)
  vapply(x, function(z) {
    parts <- strsplit(z, " ")[[1]]
    if (length(parts) >= 2 && nchar(parts[1]) > 0)
      paste0(substr(parts[1], 1, 1), ". ", parts[2]) else z
  }, character(1))
}

# Collapse weakly-supported internal branches into polytomies. This MUST match
# Figure 1 so the rebuilt tree's internal node numbering lines up with the node ids
# in the reconstruction CSV. Node support (bootstrap, 0-100) rides on $node.label;
# we zero the branches subtending below-threshold nodes and let di2multi() merge
# them. The root is never collapsed; non-numeric support is left in place.
SUPPORT_CUTOFF <- 70

collapse_low_support <- function(phy, cutoff = SUPPORT_CUTOFF) {
  if (is.null(phy$node.label)) return(phy)
  supp     <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(phy$node.label))
  internal <- (ape::Ntip(phy) + 1):(ape::Ntip(phy) + phy$Nnode)
  low      <- setdiff(internal[!is.na(supp) & supp < cutoff], ape::Ntip(phy) + 1)
  if (!length(low)) return(phy)
  phy$edge.length[phy$edge[, 2] %in% low] <- 0
  ape::di2multi(phy, tol = 1e-8)
}

# Palettes (host-use palette shared with Figure 1; ATPalpha palette matches
# Extended Data Fig. 1, where QAN is the Heliconius genotype).
full_palette <- c("none" = "grey90", "milkweed" = "#d7c0dd",
                  "asclepias" = "#65338f")
atpa_palette <- c("VSH" = "#ed1c2c", "VSN" = "#f36f21", "LSN" = "#fec12b",
                  "LAN" = "#3a6a9e", "QAN" = "grey30")
atpa_levels  <- c("VSH", "VSN", "LSN", "LAN", "QAN")
```

# 2. Rebuild the full tree and per-species states

The full tree is rebuilt exactly as in Figure 1 (collapse low-support nodes, then
rotate to the reference order) so its internal node numbers match the reconstruction.

```{r rebuild-tree}
tree_asr <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/Danaini_in_HOSTS.newick")
tree_asr$tip.label <- clean_name(tree_asr$tip.label)
tree_asr <- collapse_low_support(tree_asr)

# Orient to the curated reference order (rotation changes display only). Heliconius
# erato is absent from the reference tree, so it sits at the base with the outgroups.
reference_tree <- ape::read.tree("../input_data/danaini_reference_order.newick")
reference_tree$tip.label <- clean_name(reference_tree$tip.label)
reference_order <- {
  d <- ggtree(reference_tree, ladderize = FALSE)$data
  d <- d[d$isTip, ]
  clean_name(d$label[order(d$y, decreasing = TRUE)])
}
reference_order <- c(reference_order, "Heliconius erato")
tree_asr <- ape::rotateConstr(
  tree_asr, rev(intersect(reference_order, tree_asr$tip.label))
)

states_raw <- read.csv(
  "../input_data/danaini_host_use_states.csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>%
  mutate(butterfly_species = clean_name(butterfly_species))

# One row per tree tip; tips absent from the states table are coded "none".
host_states_tbl <- tibble(butterfly_species = tree_asr$tip.label) %>%
  left_join(states_raw, by = "butterfly_species") %>%
  mutate(
    has_milkweed         = tidyr::replace_na(as.logical(has_asclepiad_secamonoid), FALSE),
    has_asclepias_native = tidyr::replace_na(as.logical(has_asclepias_native), FALSE)
  )

# Full-tree tip order (top to bottom), reused to orient the pruned focused tree.
ref_p <- ggtree(tree_asr, ladderize = FALSE)
ref_order_top_bottom <- clean_name(
  ref_p$data$label[ref_p$data$isTip][
    order(ref_p$data$y[ref_p$data$isTip], decreasing = TRUE)
  ]
)
```

# 3. Read the whole-tree reconstruction from Figure 1

```{r read-asr}
if (!file.exists(asr_source))
  stop("Figure 1 reconstruction not found at ", asr_source,
       " — render Figure1 first.")

asr_three <- read.csv(asr_source, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

# Figure 1 writes the milkweed-clade column under its full taxonomic name; map it
# back to the short "milkweed" key this notebook uses internally (palette, pie cols).
names(asr_three)[names(asr_three) == "Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae"] <- "milkweed"

# The pie lookup below maps focused-tree nodes to full-tree node ids, so the
# reconstruction's node set must match the rebuilt tree's internal nodes exactly.
# If this fails, the two were built with different settings (e.g. a different
# SUPPORT_CUTOFF) — re-render Figure 1 and this notebook from the same inputs.
internal_nodes <- (ape::Ntip(tree_asr) + 1):(ape::Ntip(tree_asr) + tree_asr$Nnode)
stopifnot(setequal(asr_three$node, internal_nodes))
cat("Reconstruction read for", nrow(asr_three), "internal nodes; matches tree.\n")
```

# 4. Focused-subset helpers

The **focused** figure is restricted to butterflies with a known ATPα state and
reuses the whole-tree reconstruction rather than refitting on the pruned tree.

```{r helpers}
atpa_known_species <- states_raw %>%
  transmute(tip = butterfly_species,
            atpa_state = dplyr::na_if(str_squish(atpa_state), "")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(atpa_state), atpa_state != "unknown")

cat("Species with a known ATPalpha state:", nrow(atpa_known_species), "\n")

# Inner ATPalpha strip (rownames = tips) for a focused tree.
atpa_strip_for <- function(tree_f) {
  s <- atpa_known_species %>%
    filter(tip %in% tree_f$tip.label) %>%
    mutate(atpa_state = factor(atpa_state, levels = atpa_levels)) %>%
    column_to_rownames("tip")
  s[tree_f$tip.label, , drop = FALSE]
}

# Prune the full tree to the ATPalpha-known subset, re-rotated to the reference order.
focus_tree <- function(tree_src) {
  focused_tips <- intersect(atpa_known_species$tip, tree_src$tip.label)
  tf <- ape::keep.tip(tree_src, focused_tips)
  ape::rotateConstr(tf, rev(intersect(ref_order_top_bottom, tf$tip.label)))
}

# Reuse the whole-tree ASR: map each internal node of the focused (pruned) tree to
# the corresponding full-tree node (MRCA of the same tips) and copy its ancestral
# probabilities. Does NOT refit the model.
subset_asr_pies <- function(tree_full, asr_full, tree_f, cols) {
  ntip <- length(tree_f$tip.label)
  nodes_f <- (ntip + 1):(ntip + tree_f$Nnode)
  rows <- lapply(nodes_f, function(nd) {
    tips    <- ape::extract.clade(tree_f, nd)$tip.label
    full_nd <- ape::getMRCA(tree_full, tips)
    cbind(node = nd, asr_full[asr_full$node == full_nd, cols, drop = FALSE])
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

# Two host-use bars (milkweed-clade use, native-Asclepias use) on the shared
# three-level scale, for any (sub)tree.
host_bars_for <- function(tree_f) {
  host_states_tbl %>%
    filter(butterfly_species %in% tree_f$tip.label) %>%
    transmute(
      butterfly_species,
      milkweed_use  = factor(if_else(has_milkweed, "milkweed", "none"),
                             levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias")),
      asclepias_use = factor(if_else(has_asclepias_native, "asclepias", "none"),
                             levels = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias"))
    ) %>%
    column_to_rownames("butterfly_species") %>%
    { .[tree_f$tip.label, , drop = FALSE] }
}
```

# 5. Focused three-state figure (ATPα-known subset)

The two-bar figure restricted to the butterflies with a known ATPα state, with an
inner ATPα strip added. Each focused internal node reuses the whole-tree
probabilities (`asr_three`) via `subset_asr_pies()`.

```{r figure-focused, fig.width=10, fig.height=9}
tree_focused <- focus_tree(tree_asr)
asr_focused  <- subset_asr_pies(tree_asr, asr_three, tree_focused,
                                c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias"))

cat("Focused tips:", length(tree_focused$tip.label), "\n")

# Spell the milkweed-clade column out in full for the written output (the figure
# below keeps the short "milkweed" key internally).
asr_focused_out <- asr_focused %>%
  rename(`Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae` = milkweed)
write.csv(asr_focused_out,
          "../output_data/host_use_focused_ASR_node_probabilities.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

bars_f <- host_bars_for(tree_focused)
milkweed_strip  <- bars_f[, "milkweed_use",  drop = FALSE]
asclepias_strip <- bars_f[, "asclepias_use", drop = FALSE]

pf <- ggtree(tree_focused, branch.length = "none", ladderize = FALSE,
             size = 0.3, color = "grey40")
xmax_f <- max(pf$data$x, na.rm = TRUE)

# Inner strip: ATPalpha state (its own legend)
pf <- gheatmap(pf, atpa_strip_for(tree_focused), offset = 0.01, width = 0.04,
               colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = expression("ATP" * alpha * " state"),
                    values = atpa_palette, breaks = atpa_levels, drop = FALSE) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

# Two host-use bars sharing one combined legend
pf <- gheatmap(pf, milkweed_strip, offset = xmax_f * 0.06, width = 0.04,
               colnames = FALSE, color = NA)
pf <- gheatmap(pf, asclepias_strip, offset = xmax_f * 0.12, width = 0.04,
               colnames = FALSE, color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name   = "Host use",
    values = full_palette,
    breaks = c("asclepias", "milkweed", "none"),
    labels = c(expression(paste(italic("Asclepias"), " (native range)")),
               expression("Asclepiadoideae & Secamonoideae"),
               expression("Non-milkweed")),
    drop   = FALSE
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1)) +
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()

pf <- pf +
  geom_tiplab(aes(label = abbr_tip(label)), offset = xmax_f * 0.20,
              size = 3, fontface = "italic", align = TRUE, linetype = 0) +
  xlim_tree(xmax_f + 6)

pies_f <- nodepie(asr_focused, cols = c("none", "milkweed", "asclepias"), alpha = 1)
pies_f <- lapply(pies_f, function(g)
  g + scale_fill_manual(values = full_palette) + theme(legend.position = "none"))

pf_final <- inset(pf, pies_f, width = 0.05, height = 0.05) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.04, 0.98), legend.justification = c(0, 1),
        legend.box = "vertical", legend.background = element_blank(),
        legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))

pf_final
ggsave("../visuals/host_use_focused_ASR.png",
       pf_final, width = 10, height = 9)
```
